extracted.intended_audience: health journalists, consumers of health news, and supporters/donors interested in health news quality
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational mission and principles that guide evaluation of health journalism, news releases, advertising and PR, emphasizing accuracy, balance, completeness, independence, transparency, and support for shared decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy, balance and completeness about tradeoffs
rubrics_metrics.description: Promoting the principles of shared decision-making reinforced by accurate, balanced and complete information about the tradeoffs involved in health care decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HealthNewsReview.org's mission is to improve public dialogue by helping consumers critically analyze claims about health care interventions and by promoting accurate, balanced and complete information about tradeoffs; this standard is applied when evaluating health care journalism, advertising, marketing, public relations and other messages that may influence consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence from industry influence
rubrics_metrics.description: HealthNewsReview.org does not accept advertising, nor do we accept funding from any entity whose support would represent a conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Site content is presented as not influenced by any commercial interest; expert contributors pledge not to accept payments from drug or device companies or commercial entities whose support might represent a conflict. The site also maintains and uses a list of industry-independent experts for quotations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of experts' financial interests
rubrics_metrics.description: When quoting someone who’s not a member of our team, we’ll ask them about any financial interests they may have in the topic we’re writing about, and disclose those interests in the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an operational rule applied to ensure transparency when external experts are used in reviews or articles; it complements the broader independence/conflict-of-interest standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding transparency and editorial independence
rubrics_metrics.description: No funder has ever had, nor will they ever have, any editorial control over the operation of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site discloses its funders (examples given: Laura and John Arnold Foundation; Informed Medical Decisions Foundation) and explicitly states that gifts/donations will be used to support operations, while reiterating that funders do not control editorial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation — not a medical advice or advocacy body
rubrics_metrics.description: We are not equipped to host a definitive forum on medical science. We don’t give medical advice. We are not an advocacy group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets operational boundaries for the site’s reviews: the project focuses on reviewing daily health care news stories, journal practices and health care advertising/PR/marketing, rather than providing medical advice or acting as an advocacy organization. It also explains practical limits (staff size, budget) on how many items can be reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of content to be evaluated
rubrics_metrics.description: We evaluate health care journalism, advertising, marketing, public relations and other messages that may influence consumers and provides criteria that consumers can use to evaluate these messages themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies the kinds of materials the organization reviews (news stories, news releases, advertising, PR) and that the criteria they develop are intended for both the site’s reviewers and for consumers/journalists to apply independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for shared decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Promoting the principles of shared decision-making reinforced by accurate, balanced and complete information about the tradeoffs involved in health care decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organization uses shared decision-making as an evaluative lens—favoring reporting that presents benefits and harms/tradeoffs clearly so consumers can participate meaningfully in health decisions.
